summary: The quotient-residual argument correctly constructs a finite weighted graph measure on the reduced mixed-integer space, applies the accepted centerpoint theorem with the claimed dimension, pulls the center back into C by strict separation, and transfers its halfspace mass to mixed volume using the stated fiber-depth bounds. All finiteness, measurability, lattice-affine-span, zero-dimensional, boundary-halfspace, and degenerate cases used in that proof are justified. Each corollary then follows with the stated constants from the accepted metronoid and covariance facts or from the proved theorem, Markov's inequality, the spectral trace identity, convexity of the homothetic bundle, and fiberwise integration for products. No mathematical error or logical gap was found.
